definitions.gloss: buying books and leaving them unread; piling up unread books
definitions.explanation: The habit of acquiring books but letting them pile up without reading them. A playful compound blending {積|つ}む (to pile up) with {読|どく} (reading).

examples.japanese: {積|つ}ん{読|どく}がどんどん{増|ふ}える。
examples.english: My pile of unread books keeps growing.

examples.japanese: また{本|ほん}を{買|か}ってしまった。{積|つ}ん{読|どく}が{止|と}まらない。
examples.english: I bought another book. I can't stop piling up unread ones.

examples.japanese: {本棚|ほんだな}の{半分|はんぶん}は{積|つ}ん{読|どく}の{本|ほん}で{埋|う}まっている。
examples.english: Half my bookshelf is filled with books I've bought but never read.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
A playful portmanteau of {積|つ}む (to pile up) and {読|どく} (reading, from {読書|どくしょ}). The ん connects the two elements, mimicking the sound of {積|つ}んでおく (to leave piled up). The word dates to the Meiji era.

USAGE:
Used both as a noun ({積|つ}ん{読|どく}の{本|ほん}, unread books) and with する ({積|つ}ん{読|どく}する). The word carries a self-deprecating, humorous tone — book lovers use it to describe their own habit. It has been borrowed into English as "tsundoku."

RELATED WORDS:
- {精読|せいどく} (close reading)
- {多読|たどく} (extensive reading)
- {読書|どくしょ} (reading books)
